title: Titanium Seatpost Collar Bolt

This rationale is driven by seatpost collar quick-release binder bolt and specific design requirements.

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Seatpost Collar Bolt suitable for Seatpost collar quick-release binder bolt?
faq.a: Titanium Seatpost Collar Bolt uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address seat hardware operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Seatpost Collar Bolt?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Seatpost Collar Bolt require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. seat hardware components receive Bead blasting 120 grit Al2O3 for matte finish Ra 1.6-3.2um followed by passive oxide stabilization in DI water. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the service environment.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Seatpost Collar Bolt shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements; (4) Surface roughness certification on critical features. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Seatpost clamp / Collar bolt seat hardware components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
